title: Anthropic Prices IPO at $83 a Share, Valuing Claude Maker at About $1.5 Trillion
excerpt: The biggest debut on record prices above its range and starts trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT — with a filing that shows rapid revenue growth alongside heavy losses and nearly $900 billion in computing commitments.
body:
• Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above its $70 to $78 target range, raising $81.31 billion and valuing the company at about $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, Reuters reported.
  • Shares are expected to start trading on Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, alongside a separate $26 billion private placement at the IPO price.
  • The prospectus shows an annualized revenue run rate of $81 billion as of October 31, but also a third-quarter net loss of $23.3 billion and nearly $900 billion in committed computing spending.
  • Anthropic is the first major frontier AI model developer to go public; OpenAI is also expected to pursue a listing as early as next year, Reuters reported.

Anthropic, the company behind the Claude chatbot, has priced the largest stock-market debut on record. The offering was priced at $83 a share on Wednesday, above the $70 to $78 range the company had targeted, and raised $81.31 billion, eclipsing SpaceX's offering earlier this year, Reuters reported. On a fully diluted basis the price values Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion, including securities such as stock options and restricted stock; on a non-diluted basis the valuation is about $1.1 trillion.

Reuters was first to report that the IPO was upsized by about 19 percent to 980 million shares, from an initial plan to sell 825 million shares. Anthropic is also raising $26 billion through a private placement at the IPO price, its filings show. Shares are expected to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT — the same day Asian equities and US stock futures rose after the pricing, according to Reuters' markets wrap. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead underwriters, heading a 22-bank syndicate.

Growth, as filed

The growth in the prospectus is steep. Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing. The company had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year. Revenue rose 47 percent in the third quarter to $16.96 billion from the second quarter, driven by demand for its Claude models — particularly Claude Code, its coding agent.

The cost of staying at the frontier

The same filing shows what that growth costs. Anthropic reported an operating loss of $567 million in the third quarter, against operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter. Its net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating items related to bonds convertible into its shares. The company spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026 — nearly four times the amount a year earlier — and a further $5 billion in the third quarter. It has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google, and warned in its prospectus that if financing for those partners becomes unavailable or more costly, "contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered."

"The vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier."

— Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, to Reuters

Competition and what to watch

Anthropic arrives on the market as competition intensifies. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra accounted for about 13 percent of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8 percent for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September, and a Capgemini study found 59 percent of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year. OpenAI is also expected to pursue a public listing as early as next year. The first test is Thursday's opening trade: whether public investors price the frontier at $1.5 trillion, or mark it down the way SpaceX's shares were marked down in the weeks after its debut.
